keyTakeaways: Halloween around the world splits three ways: a main event in the US, Canada, Ireland and the UK; the eve of All Saints' and All Souls' Days in Catholic Europe and Latin America; and a side event in Asia, where lunar festivals of the dead come weeks earlier.

Hard numbers are rare: the US Census counts 73.1 million potential trick-or-treaters, while YouGov found 51% of adults in Great Britain don't celebrate; most of the 23 countries here have no national survey.

The Hungry Ghost Festival falls on 27 August 2026 and 16 August 2027, and Pitru Paksha runs 26 September–10 October 2026 and 15–29 September 2027, so Asia's nights for spirits usually come before 31 October.
Late October is also an anniversary in South Korea: the 29 October 2022 Itaewon crush killed 158 people by a 2023 peer-reviewed count, later 159.
SubhSandesh miss-you senders name 47 distinct city pairs, including Mumbai-London; 48.3% of page views are on phones, so a greeting to a friend abroad should be phone-first.

faqs.question: Which countries celebrate Halloween the most?
faqs.answer: The US, Canada, Ireland and the UK treat 31 October as a major night. The US Census Bureau counts 73.1 million American children under 18 as potential trick-or-treaters, and a 2025 Narrative Research poll found half of Canadian adults hand out treats. Even in Britain, YouGov's 2025 poll found 51% of adults don't celebrate.

faqs.question: Is Día de Muertos the Mexican version of Halloween?
faqs.answer: No. Día de Muertos on 1–2 November is a remembrance of family dead with home altars, food and photographs, rooted in All Saints' and All Souls' Days. Anthropologist Stanley Brandes documented how Halloween costumes spread into Mexico in the 1990s and how some Mexicans pushed back to protect the older feast.

faqs.question: Do people in China celebrate Halloween?
faqs.answer: Mostly as costume parties for young adults in big cities, where it is called Wànshèngjié and seen as foreign. China's own night for wandering spirits is the Hungry Ghost Festival on the 15th night of the seventh lunar month, which falls on 27 August 2026 and 16 August 2027.

faqs.question: Is Halloween a public holiday anywhere?
faqs.answer: We found no country where 31 October itself is a Halloween holiday. Nearby days are: Reformation Day on 31 October is a holiday in 9 German states, All Saints' Day on 1 November is a public holiday in France, Italy, Spain and Poland, and the Philippines declares 1–2 November special non-working days.

faqs.question: Is Halloween banned in any country?
faqs.answer: We could not verify a current national ban. Saudi Arabia is the clearest change on record: NDTV reported a 2018 police raid on a Halloween party, then a public 'scary weekend' in Riyadh in 2022 under Vision 2030. For the rest of the Middle East we found no reliable data.

faqs.question: What happened at Itaewon on Halloween 2022?
faqs.answer: On 29 October 2022, Halloween crowds were trapped in a narrow, sloping alley in Itaewon, Seoul. A 2023 peer-reviewed review by Kyoo-Man Ha records 158 deaths, 26 of them foreign nationals, and 196 injured; later official counts reached 159. Late October in South Korea is now also an anniversary.

faqs.question: What is Dia do Saci in Brazil?
faqs.answer: Dia do Saci is a 31 October commemoration of the Saci, a one-legged trickster from Brazilian folklore, promoted as a homegrown alternative to Halloween. São Paulo state made it official with Law 11,669 of 13 January 2004; it is a commemorative date, not a day off.

faqs.question: Which country celebrates Halloween first?
faqs.answer: Places at UTC+14, such as Kiribati's Line Islands, reach 31 October first. Among countries where Halloween is commonly marked, New Zealand, at UTC+13 in daylight-saving time, is one of the first; a greeting sent at 7 pm Delhi time lands there at 2:30 am the next day.

faqs.question: What is Undas in the Philippines?
faqs.answer: Undas is the Filipino name for the 1–2 November days when families travel home to visit and clean their relatives' graves. Proclamation No. 1006 made both days special non-working days for 2026, and Proclamation No. 1427 does the same for 2027, according to its preamble.

faqs.question: How can I wish a friend abroad a happy Halloween?
faqs.answer: Check their time zone first: 7 pm in Delhi is 9:30 am in New York and 1:30 pm in London on 31 October. For one close friend, SubhSandesh's Halloween page has a bestie mode with up to six photos and a downloadable Boo License; skip it if they are mourning or read no English.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Halloween Around the World: Who Celebrates It and How

Halloween around the world splits three ways. In the US, Canada, Ireland and the UK, 31 October is the main event; across Catholic Europe and Latin America it is the night before the 1–2 November feasts for saints and souls; and in much of Asia the big nights for the dead fall on lunar dates weeks earlier. Below: 23 countries and regions with names, dates, reach and customs.

Where no national survey exists, the entry says so. These greetings cross borders too: on SubhSandesh's miss-you template, senders name 47 distinct city pairs, including Mumbai-London and Berlin-London, and 48.3% of SubhSandesh views arrive via phones.

## Who celebrates Halloween in the world?

Halloween is 31 October, the vigil before the church's holy day for all saints. Outside its Irish, Scottish and North American heartland it is mostly a recent import, carried by trade and television rather than churches.

Anthropologist Stanley Brandes traced that route in a [2000 study of Mexico in *Alteridades*](https://www.redalyc.org/articulo.oa?id=74702002), linking shop-bought costumes and plastic pumpkins to NAFTA (ratified 1993), returning migrants and American television. He also recorded the pushback: a Tepoztlán mural reading "No al Halloween. Conserva tus tradiciones" ("No to Halloween. Keep your traditions"), and an Oaxaca altar contest that disqualified foreign elements.

## How Halloween is celebrated in 23 countries, region by region

Each entry gives five fields: name, date, reach, related festival and custom. "No national survey" means we found no representative poll, not that nobody takes part.

### The Americas: 4 countries

- **United States.** *Name:* Halloween. *Date:* 31 October (Saturday 2026, Sunday 2027). *Reach:* the [US Census Bureau's 2025 Halloween fact sheet](https://www.census.gov/newsroom/facts-for-features/2025/halloween.html) counts 73.1 million children under 18 as potential trick-or-treaters. *Related:* none. *Custom:* door-to-door trick-or-treating.
- **Canada.** *Name:* Halloween; l'Halloween in Quebec. *Date:* 31 October. *Reach:* a Narrative Research online poll of 1,230 adults (October 2025) found half hand out treats, but only 34% in Quebec. *Related:* none. *Custom:* a Kingston, Ontario newspaper described children "guising" in 1911.
- **Mexico.** *Name:* Halloween, then Día de Muertos. *Date:* 1–2 November, not a federal rest day. *Reach:* no national survey; Brandes saw children begging among graves for their "jalouín". *Related:* Día de Muertos, a remembrance of family dead, not a Mexican Halloween. *Custom:* home altars (*ofrendas*) with flowers, food and photographs.
- **Brazil.** *Name:* Dia das Bruxas ("Witches' Day"). *Date:* 31 October; Dia de Finados, 2 November, is a national holiday. *Reach:* no national survey. *Related:* Dia do Saci, fixed on 31 October by [São Paulo state Law 11,669 of 13 January 2004](https://www.al.sp.gov.br/repositorio/legislacao/lei/2004/lei-11669-13.01.2004.html). *Custom:* honouring the Saci, a one-legged folklore trickster.

### Europe: 8 countries

- **Ireland.** *Name:* Oíche Shamhna. *Date:* 31 October; the bank holiday is 26 October 2026 and 25 October 2027. *Reach:* no national survey verified here. *Related:* Samhain. *Custom:* barmbrack, a fruit loaf with a ring baked inside.
- **United Kingdom.** *Name:* Halloween. *Date:* 31 October; Bonfire Night, 5 November. *Reach:* in [YouGov's September 2025 poll of 2,069 adults](https://yougov.com/en-gb/articles/53067-uk-halloween-spending-shopping-trends-2025), 51% in Great Britain don't celebrate. *Related:* Bonfire Night. *Custom:* Scottish guising, a joke or song before sweets.
- **Germany.** *Name:* Halloween. *Date:* 31 October is also Reformation Day, a holiday in 9 of 16 states; All Saints is a holiday in 5. *Reach:* no national survey; it spread from the 1990s. *Related:* Allerheiligen. *Custom:* the rhyme "Süßes, sonst gibt's Saures" ("sweets, or it turns sour").
- **France.** *Name:* Halloween. *Date:* La Toussaint, 1 November, is a public holiday. *Reach:* no national survey; a late-1990s retail boom cooled. *Related:* Toussaint. *Custom:* Brittany's Kalan Goañv, an older night of returning dead.
- **Italy.** *Name:* Halloween. *Date:* Ognissanti, 1 November, is a public holiday. *Reach:* no national survey. *Related:* Ognissanti and 2 November. *Custom:* Sardinia's *concas de mortu*, pumpkins carved as skulls.
- **Spain.** *Name:* Halloween. *Date:* Todos los Santos, 1 November, is a national holiday. *Reach:* no national survey. *Related:* Todos los Santos. *Custom:* Catalonia's Castanyada: roasted chestnuts and *panellets*, almond sweets rolled in pine nuts.
- **Poland.** *Name:* Halloween. *Date:* 1 November is a public holiday; Zaduszki follows on 2 November. *Reach:* no national survey; growing among young people since 1989, mostly as parties. *Related:* Zaduszki. *Custom:* cemeteries lit with candles.
- **Sweden.** *Name:* Halloween. *Date:* Alla helgons dag is the Saturday between 31 October and 6 November: 31 October 2026, 6 November 2027. *Reach:* no national survey; children's costumes caught on around 2005. *Related:* Alla helgons dag. *Custom:* candles and pine wreaths on graves.

### Asia: 7 countries and territories

- **Philippines.** *Name:* Undas. *Date:* Proclamation No. 1006 makes All Saints' Day a special (non-working) day and adds All Souls' Day, Monday 2 November, for 2026; No. 1427 lists Monday 1 November 2027, and its preamble adds Tuesday 2 November. *Reach:* no national survey; families travel home to visit graves. *Related:* Undas. *Custom:* *pangangaluluwa*, singing house to house for the souls.
- **China (mainland).** *Name:* Wànshèngjié (万圣节, "All Saints' Festival"). *Date:* 31 October, no holiday. *Reach:* no national survey; city costume parties, widely seen as foreign. *Related:* the Hungry Ghost Festival. *Custom:* floating river lanterns for the dead.
- **Hong Kong.** *Name:* Halloween. *Date:* 31 October, no holiday. *Reach:* no survey; high-rise living makes door-to-door rare. *Related:* Yu Lan, the Hungry Ghost Festival. *Custom:* costume crowds in Lan Kwai Fong.
- **Japan.** *Name:* Harowīn. *Date:* 31 October, no holiday. *Reach:* no national survey; an adult costume night without trick-or-treating. *Related:* Obon, mid-August. *Custom:* street costume crowds.
- **South Korea.** *Name:* Haelleowin (핼러윈). *Date:* 31 October, no holiday. *Reach:* no national survey; spread through English academies and marketing. *Related:* Chuseok (24–26 September 2026; 14–16 September 2027). *Custom:* since 2022, late October is also a memorial.
- **India.** *Name:* Halloween. *Date:* 31 October, no holiday. *Reach:* no survey; club and house parties in big cities. *Related:* Pitru Paksha, 26 September–10 October 2026 and 15–29 September 2027 (New Delhi, Drik Panchang). *Custom:* food offerings to ancestors.
- **Nepal.** *Name:* none in common use. *Date:* not observed nationally. *Reach:* no data. *Related:* Gai Jatra, August or September, for relatives who died that year. *Custom:* children dressed as cows join the procession.

### Oceania: 2 countries

- **Australia.** *Name:* Halloween. *Date:* 31 October, in spring. *Reach:* retail estimates only; no state makes it a holiday. *Related:* none. *Custom:* daylight trick-or-treating.
- **New Zealand.** *Name:* Halloween. *Date:* 31 October; at UTC+13 it is among the first countries to reach it. *Reach:* no national survey; it grew from the 1990s. *Related:* none. *Custom:* children's trick-or-treating.

### Africa and the Middle East: limited data

- **Nigeria and sub-Saharan Africa.** *Name:* Halloween. *Date:* 31 October. *Reach:* no survey, statute or dated report found. *Related and custom:* not verified, so left blank.
- **Saudi Arabia and the Gulf.** *Name:* Halloween. *Date:* 31 October. *Reach:* no survey. *Related:* none. *Custom:* [NDTV reported on 2 November 2022](https://web.archive.org/web/20221121031803/https://www.ndtv.com/world-news/saudi-arabia-celebrates-halloween-internet-gives-mixed-reaction-3480989) a Thursday-to-Sunday "scary weekend" in Riyadh, allowed under Vision 2030 after years of prohibition. Elsewhere in the region: no reliable data.

## Halloween around the world at a glance: 5 regions compared

This table condenses the 23 entries into five regions.

| Region | Celebrated on 31 October? | Local festival of the dead | Signature custom |
|---|---|---|---|
| Americas | US, Canada: yes; Mexico, Brazil: growing, no survey | Día de Muertos 1–2 Nov; Finados 2 Nov | Trick-or-treating; *ofrendas* |
| Europe | Ireland, UK: yes, though 51% of GB adults abstain | All Saints, 1 Nov: national holiday in 5 of 8 | Candles on graves |
| Asia | City parties; no national survey anywhere | Hungry Ghost 27 Aug 2026; Pitru Paksha from 26 Sep 2026; Undas | Lanterns, food offerings |
| Oceania | Yes, smaller, in spring | None | Daylight trick-or-treating |
| Africa and Middle East | Limited; Riyadh public events since 2021 | Not verified | Riyadh "scary weekend" |

Wherever an older remembrance exists, Halloween plays second fiddle.

## Why some festivals of the dead fall weeks before 31 October

Halloween keeps a fixed Gregorian date, but most Asian festivals of the dead follow the moon. The Hungry Ghost Festival is the 15th night of the seventh Chinese lunar month: Thursday 27 August 2026 and Monday 16 August 2027.

Pitru Paksha ends on Sarva Pitru Amavasya, 10 October 2026 and 29 September 2027, and Chuseok in 2027 ends about six weeks before Halloween. So "Halloween in China" or "in India" usually means an imported party, held after the local night of spirits.

## Where Halloween sits beside grief or restriction

Late on 29 October 2022, Halloween crowds packed a sloping Itaewon alley in Seoul, 40 metres long and 4 metres wide. A [2023 F1000Research review by Kyoo-Man Ha](https://f1000research.com/articles/12-829/v2) records 158 deaths, 26 of them foreign nationals, and 196 injured; later official counts reached 159.

For a Korean friend, late October is an anniversary first. In the Philippines and Mexico, 1–2 November means cemetery visits, so keep jokes to 31 October. In Saudi Arabia, NDTV recalls a 2018 police raid on a Halloween party; check local rules before posting publicly.

## Greeting a friend abroad on 31 October: time zones first

A link sent from Delhi at 7 pm on Halloween reaches New York at 9:30 am, London at 1:30 pm and Auckland at 2:30 am the next day; the clocks give the same result for 2026 and 2027. For Auckland, send by 10:30 am Delhi time to land at 6 pm.

For one far-off friend, pick bestie on SubhSandesh's [Halloween greeting page](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween) and the final question reworks itself for friendship. Load six pictures at most, plus the word that glows inside the carved pumpkin; they tour a pocket-sized haunted house, read your note by torch in the attic, and save a portrait Boo License, 1080 by 1920 pixels.

Opening it takes only a browser, and you hear by email once they answer. Over every SubhSandesh page, the mean is 11.1 views apiece, and 38.5% of makers set a password. If that person overseas is a partner, the [I-miss-you page with a reunion countdown](https://subhsandesh.in/missyou-gf) fits better.

## Grief, language and crowds: 3 reasons to hold the card

Skip it for anyone mourning: a friend at an Undas grave, building an *ofrenda*, or in Korea near 29 October. Write plain words; SubhSandesh has no remembrance template, and the [full template list](https://subhsandesh.in/templates) won't change that.

Buttons and prompts appear only in English, so a friend who reads just Korean or Portuguese will see English controls. Each card has one recipient; it cannot gather party guests.

- São Paulo Law 11,669, 13 January 2004
- YouGov, 6 October 2025
- NDTV, 2 November 2022 (archived)
- Ha, *F1000Research*, 22 November 2023

structuralLimitations: Prompt said 'USA (scale stat from NRF; nrf.com is fresh in b4)'. BRIEF §5 (binding) allows nrf.com ONLY for spending/budget/gifts/costume posts; this hub is none of those, so the US scale figure comes from the US Census Bureau 2025 Halloween fact sheet instead (the one generic statistic).

Proclamation No. 1427 (2027 holidays) on Lawphil: the preamble declares 2 November 2027 an 'additional special (non-working) day', but the rendered table lists All Souls' Day 2 November (Tuesday) under the 'C. Special (Working) Day' heading, apparently a missing 'D. Additional special (non-working) days' heading. The post cites the preamble only. The b4 Tagalog sibling states 1 and 2 November 2027 are both non-working; worth an Official Gazette check (officialgazette.gov.ph returned 403 to that sibling). Proclamations 1006/1427 are named in the body but not linked, to keep outbound links at 6 (both URLs are in the Tagalog sibling).

Dia do Saci (prompt: 'verify'): verified as a São Paulo STATE commemorative date (Law 11,669 of 13 January 2004, fetched from al.sp.gov.br). English Wikipedia's 'official holiday in the state of São Paulo' overstates it: the law only institutes a date to be commemorated. pt.wikipedia says the national bill PL 2479/2003 was archived in 2008 (not independently fetched from camara.leg.br, so the body no longer states it).

Itaewon toll: Ha 2023 (F1000Research) gives 158 dead (132 Korean, 26 foreign) and 196 injured; English Wikipedia gives 159 including later deaths and 27 foreign nationals. The post states Ha's 158 and 'later official counts reached 159'.

timeanddate.com returned 403 (bot wall, not worked around). Public-holiday statements (Germany: Reformation Day in 9 states, All Saints in 5; Poland, Spain, Italy, France, Sweden, Brazil Finados, Ireland October bank holiday; none for Mexico, Hong Kong, South Korea, China on 25 Oct–3 Nov) were verified against the Nager.Date public holiday API (date.nager.at), not cited. Pitru Paksha dates from Drik Panchang with New Delhi location (26 Sep–10 Oct 2026; 15–29 Sep 2027); with the default Orlando location the page shows a day earlier for 2026. Hungry Ghost dates (27 Aug 2026, 16 Aug 2027) were computed from the ICU Chinese calendar (Intl.DateTimeFormat 'en-u-ca-chinese'), not fetched from an almanac.

Unlinked, verified claims kept to hold outbound links at 6: Canada 'half hand out treats, 34% in Quebec' (Narrative Research, 1,230 adults, 7–9 Oct 2025, fetched; the b4 Canada sibling cites it); Kingston, Ontario 1911 guising report, Germany/Poland/Italy/Sweden/Hong Kong/China/NZ/Korea context lines (English Wikipedia 'Geography of Halloween', read via API, not linked); Japan and Australia lines summarise the b3/b2 sibling posts.

Nigeria / sub-Saharan Africa: no survey, statute or dated report found; the entry says so and leaves 'related festival' and 'custom' blank rather than copying listicle claims (mentalfloss, a top-5 competitor, lists Awuru Odo; not used). Middle East beyond Saudi Arabia: no reliable data; NDTV live page 403, read via Wayback Machine.

failed.item: At least one table column uses first-party data
failed.why: No Halloween usage data exists in content/facts.md (BRIEF §3/§9), and platform-wide lines (phone share, views per page) do not vary by country of recipient, so a first-party column in a country/region table would be decoration. Structural: re-check when facts.md carries per-country or per-template Halloween counts for /happy-halloween after 31 October.

failed.item: No source passes the **swap test** — none could sit unchanged in a different keyword's post in this batch
failed.why: The US Census Bureau Halloween fact sheet (73.1 million potential trick-or-treaters) is the post's one generic context statistic and could sit unchanged in any trick-or-treat post in this batch; the YouGov GB poll could too. They are kept because the global hub must give a sourced 'how widely' figure for the US and UK, and BRIEF §5 bars nrf.com for non-spending posts. Structural for a country-reach hub; the remaining four sources (Brandes, Ha, São Paulo Law 11,669, NDTV Riyadh) are subject-specific.

auditReport.honestAssessment: Answer engines get one thing here the analysed pages lack: every country carries the same five fields with an explicit evidence level, plus 2026 and 2027 dates for the Hungry Ghost Festival, Pitru Paksha and Chuseok and a respectful, sourced treatment of Itaewon, Undas and Día de Muertos; the five top pages (V&A, Mental Floss, Globe Trottin' Kids, Collette, The Manitoban) are undated, unsourced trivia lists. It still cannot overcome the V&A's and Mental Floss's domain authority, and most country entries honestly say 'no national survey', which is accurate but gives fewer quotable numbers than a confident listicle; expect months, not weeks.
